research_result.description: Shopify is an ecommerce platform providing extensive APIs, developer tools, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to build commerce integrations, custom storefronts, and AI-powered shopping agents.
research_result.credential_requirements: Developers obtain client credentials (client ID / SHOPIFY_API_KEY and client secret / SHOPIFY_API_SECRET) via the Dev Dashboard or Shopify CLI. These credentials are used to obtain access tokens via OAuth grants (such as token exchange or client credentials grant) to authenticate requests.

evidence.claim: Shopify supports OAuth 2.0 for API authentication.
Shopify uses API keys and client credentials to identify and authorize apps.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Some tools and documentation call these the API key and API secret: `SHOPIFY_API_KEY` holds your client ID, and `SHOPIFY_API_SECRET` holds your client secret.

evidence.claim: Shopify provides a REST Admin API.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The REST Admin API is a legacy API as of October 1, 2024.

evidence.claim: Shopify provides a GraphQL Admin API as its primary API.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: GraphQL has become Shopify's technology of choice for building APIs.

evidence.claim: Shopify offers Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to build AI shopping experiences.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Connect any AI assistant to real-time commerce data from Shopify stores with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

evidence.claim: Developers can use the Dev Dashboard as a central hub for building apps and managing test stores.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: The Dev Dashboard is your central hub for building on Shopify.

evidence.claim: Shopify provides a broad API surface across store data, customer accounts, storefronts, and extensions.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Build apps that extend and interact with the Shopify admin. Access products, customers, orders, inventory, and more.
